Cli.Help:
GARbro — browse and extract game resources

Commands:
  formats                  Show supported formats
  probe FILE               Identify an archive, image, audio or video
  list FILE                List archive entries
  extract FILE... -o DIR   Extract archives
  create INPUT... -o FILE  Create an archive
  convert FILE -o FILE     Convert an image, audio or video
  schemes FILE             Import a format database

Use garbro COMMAND --help for options and examples.
Images: PNG, WEBP (lossless), BMP, JPEG, TIFF, TGA and registered writers.
Audio: WAV, FLAC, M4A; video: MP4, MKV.

Global options: --language auto|en-US|zh-CN|ru-RU|ja-JP, --json,
  --timeout SECONDS, --max-memory BYTES, --version
--recursive traverses disk directories; --nested expands child archives.
Source files are preserved. Default limits: 300 seconds, 1 GiB memory.

Cli.Help.extract:
garbro extract FILE... -o DIRECTORY [OPTIONS]

Examples:
  garbro extract data.xfl -o extracted
  garbro extract game --recursive -o extracted
  garbro extract data.xfl --nested --image-format webp --discard-original-media -o extracted

  --recursive                  Traverse disk subfolders; skip unrecognized files
  --nested                     Also unpack child archives (shared limits)
  --image-format FORMAT        PNG, WEBP, BMP, JPEG, TIFF, TGA, or a writable tag
  --audio-format FORMAT        AUTO, WAV, FLAC, M4A
  --video-format FORMAT        MP4 (re-encode), MKV (copy streams)
  --discard-child-archives     Remove output copies only after successful --nested
  --discard-original-media     Omit original output copies after successful conversion
  --overwrite fail|skip|replace (default: fail)
  --encoding CODEPAGE          Filename/text encoding; default: automatic
  --format TAG                 Force input archive format (ordinary extraction only)
  --options FILE, --scheme NAME, --schemes FILE
  --max-depth N, --max-entry BYTES, --max-total BYTES, --max-ratio N

Source files are never deleted. Disk scans preserve relative folders.
Nested archive roots use <full filename>.unpacked; child copies stay on failure.

Cli.Help.convert:
garbro convert FILE -o OUTPUT_FILE [--to FORMAT]

Examples:
  garbro convert image.png -o image.webp
  garbro convert voice.ogg -o voice.flac
  garbro convert movie.mpg -o movie.mp4

The output extension selects the format; --to overrides it.
Images: PNG, WEBP (lossless, with alpha), BMP, JPEG, TIFF, TGA and writable tags.
Audio: WAV, FLAC, M4A; video: MP4 (MPEG-4/AAC), MKV (copy streams).
JPG/TIF/AAC are aliases for JPEG/TIFF/M4A. Format names ignore case.
Scripts: GSC → TSC, RPYC → RPY, KS → KS, TJS → TJS, BGI → BSD/BPD,
  nscript.dat → TXT, AST → AST, ASB → JSON, data.dsm → TXT, Scripts.rxdata/rvdata/rvdata2 → RB.
Use --entry NAME to convert an archive entry.
--overwrite fail|skip|replace, --format INPUT_IMAGE_TAG, --max-pixels N,
--max-entry BYTES, --encoding CODEPAGE, --options FILE, --scheme NAME.
Choose a separate output file; conversion never replaces the source.

Cli.Help.create:
garbro create INPUT... -o ARCHIVE [OPTIONS]

Examples:
  garbro create assets -o data.xfl
  garbro create image.png voice.mp3 -o data.xp3 --format XP3 --scheme none
  garbro create assets -o data.zip --image-format webp --audio-format wav --discard-original-media

Directories include subfolders. Only explicitly selected inputs are packed.
One directory uses its contents as the root; multiple inputs use their common parent.
  --format TAG_OR_ID       Writable archive format; inferred only for a unique extension
  --options FILE          JSON creation parameters for the archive writer
  --scheme NAME, --schemes FILE, --encoding CODEPAGE
  --image-format FORMAT   PNG, WEBP, BMP, JPEG, TIFF, TGA or a writable image tag
  --audio-format FORMAT   AUTO, WAV, FLAC, M4A
  --video-format FORMAT   MP4, MKV
  --discard-original-media  Pack converted media without original copies
  --overwrite fail|skip|replace (default: fail)
  --max-entry BYTES, --max-total BYTES, --timeout SECONDS, --max-memory BYTES
  --json                  Output path, format, written, entries, converted and bytes

By default media stays unchanged. Conversions retain originals unless omitted.
A conversion failure or name conflict cancels the whole archive; sources and the
previous output are preserved. Changing media formats does not update game scripts.
